newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast crude rises with WTI, diffs flat.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast crude rises with WTI, diffs flat.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices rose with November West Texas Intermediate (WTI), while differentials remained notionally unchanged in early trade.
November WTI traded stronger at $24.35/24.45 a barrel, recovering from losses of 30 cents early.
Traders waited for weekly stock data from the American Petroleum Institute, due out late Tuesday.
A Reuter survey of analysts forecast crude stocks would fall 1.50 million barrels for the week ended September 27.
Some analysts saw distillates up 1.80 million barrels and gasoline higher by 0.63 million barrels.
A major producer was expected to announce its offer for Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude today. Their last official offer was seen at $2.00 under November WTI for October delivery.
Line 63 remained unchanged at $3.20 to $3.00 under spot WTI for November delivery.
Kern River, from California's San Joaquin Valley, was unchanged at $16.15/16.35 a barrel.
And prices for Long Beach-based Wilmington crude held at $17.60/17.70.
